_doc: Known Windows test failures, recorded so the ci.yml windows job can gate on everything else. Every test listed here still RUNS on every Windows row, in a separate advisory step that reports it as a warning; it just does not fail the job. A test NOT listed for a skill that fails on Windows fails the job. Two shapes: 'failures' maps each skill to the exact tests observed failing there (the default), and 'slugs': ['*'] with 'tests' applies to every connector (only for press-generated tests every connector inherits). Remove an entry when its fix lands; the advisory step prints a notice when every listed test for a skill passes. Read by tools/maintainer/windows_known_failures.py.

entries.why: The Windows credential-permission check (internal/cliutil/creds_perms_eval.go, press 4.30.2 and later) compares SDDL text from GetNamedSecurityInfo + ConvertSecurityDescriptorToStringSecurityDescriptor against the user's SID string. Observed on windows-latest, whose account is the built-in local Administrator (whoami: S-1-5-21-...-500): the native converter renders that account as the alias LA, so the user's own ACE never matches. Production path, measured 2026-10-15 with the published fortinet-cli 0.1.0 installed by the README one-liner: `auth set-token` exits 1 with 'credentials file saved but permissions are unsafe ... token file DACL grants access to a non-owner principal (LA)'. In the tests the sandbox sets the owner explicitly, so the same alias trips the owner check instead. Anyone working as the built-in Administrator (common on MSP servers and jump boxes) cannot persist credentials; ordinary accounts are unaffected.
entries.fix: Press: compare SIDs, not SDDL strings (resolve two-letter aliases with ConvertStringSidToSid, or walk the ACL with EqualSid), and add an LA case to TestEvalCredsSecurity; then reprint or hand-fix creds_perms_eval.go per connector. Fleet-wide on purpose: these are press-generated tests every 4.30.2+ connector inherits, so a per-skill list would red each new factory connector over a defect already diagnosed. An older connector that carries a same-named test that passes loses gating on it; that is the accepted cost.

entries.why: Hand-written tests that save or mint a token, so they hit WIN-CREDS-RID500-ALIAS through the generated check. sophos-central's list also carries tests that fail downstream of the refused saves (for example TestTenantPlaceholderIsUnset reads a tenant left in the shared runner profile); suspected, not traced one by one.
entries.fix: Fixed by the WIN-CREDS-RID500-ALIAS fix; re-run and remove whatever then passes.

entries.why: Press 4.30.1 internal/platform/profile.go refuses any client profile whose Unix mode is not 0600; Windows always reports 0666. Inert today (no tenant identity adapter is registered), and fatal for client profiles once one is.
entries.fix: Reprint on press 4.30.2 or later, which splits the check into perms_windows.go.

entries.why: The test asserts a Unix permission bit (Perm() == 0o600) or relies on a read-only directory refusing writes; Windows reports 0666 and ignores read-only on directories.
entries.fix: Guard the assert with runtime.GOOS != "windows" (or assert the Windows ACL instead).

entries.why: The test isolates the store by setting only HOME. On Windows os.UserHomeDir reads USERPROFILE, so the code reads the runner's real profile (and tests pollute each other through it).
entries.fix: Set USERPROFILE alongside HOME, or use the press testenv.Isolate helper.

entries.why: Eight helper processes write one store at once; one exited 4 (a non-busy write error) on Windows. The same generated test passed in the 12 other connectors that carry it, so this reads as load-dependent, not deterministic.
entries.fix: Have the helper print its error before exiting 4, then re-run; if it reproduces, it is the CLI and MCP server writing one store concurrently on Windows.

entries.why: Not Windows-specific: the test seeds an expiry at now - 5 days with one-second resolution and the command floors days_left later, so crossing a second boundary in between yields -6. The slower Windows runner crosses it often (run 2, 2026-10-15); no other job runs go test, so it surfaced here.
entries.fix: Seed from a fixed clock, or compute the expectation from the same now the command uses.
